rules: Commands affecting one desktop must run sequentially, including screenshots taken after actions.
ok reports command execution; assert data.exists, data.conditionMet or an application postcondition separately.
verified is null when verification was not requested; successful input delivery does not prove the expected result.
Selectors are case-insensitive literal/wildcard matches by default. -Regex accepts regular expressions, not wildcard syntax.
TimeoutMs bounds retries; an individual UI Automation provider call may exceed it.
Use -Flag=value for values starting with a dash. Negative numeric values also work as separate tokens.

GuiNavigation is the default: bounded press-key navigation and audited focused literal input use the GUI. Explicit VisibleControls stays strict and forbids press-key. Application hotkeys/Shortcut clearing require authorized AllowShortcuts; clipboard is unsupported.
Commands use a bounded desktop mutex. DesktopBusy means not dispatched; outcome unknown requires observing the postcondition before retry.
Invalid bounds are returned as null with boundsStatus/propertyErrors; do not infer missing UIA support from missing geometry.

UIA bounds, screenshots and mouse points use physical screen pixels in every transport. Desktop commands temporarily set thread DPI awareness and restore it afterwards. Screenshot region.x/y is the image origin; never copy coordinates from a resized preview.

help.notes: Read command guidance without a desktop session or state mutation. Topics combines several commands with one copy of shared rules; avoid separate process starts for each topic.

state.notes: Clear resets CLI context, not application state.

start.notes: Executable launches only. RequireNewWindow (framework default) snapshots desktop handles and waits for a new visible window of the executable, including handoff to an existing process. Returns ownedProcessId/start time for a new host or ownedWindow for a shared host. Never claims an old window or a short-lived launcher PID. No new window is an error; inspect windows and deliberately focus the intended window. RequireNewProcess remains available for strict isolation; do not combine the two modes or KillExisting. A bare document/path/URL in Arguments and shell/protocol launcher wrappers bypass the GUI Open route and are rejected. Launch the executable, then use its visible Open route. Values starting with a dash must use -Arguments=<value> in one token.

focus.exactSelection: WindowSelectorJson selects exact observed Name/ClassName with optional ProcessId/NativeWindowHandle; windows -Foreground returns all four. This distinguishes same-title windows in one process without cleanup ownership. Refresh after a title/window transition. WindowIdentityJson instead requires the complete ownedWindow lifetime-token receipt. Do not interchange them. Focus rejects conflicting filters and never ignores WindowSelectorJson.
focus.notes: Explicitly switch to one observed window; ambiguous selectors fail. Plain focus does not grant cleanup ownership. For a GUI action that opens another application, first windows -Checkpoint, perform the visible action, then focus -SinceCheckpoint <returned checkpointId> with an observed unique selector. Only a window absent from that baseline receives ownedWindow for cleanup. CLI state retains the last 16 checkpoints across clients; a later diagnostic snapshot does not invalidate the pre-action ID. Take a fresh baseline before the next handoff. If a matching window existed before opening, plain focus deliberately reuses it without ownership; never pre-close all application windows or claim an old window for cleanup. Shared/window-scoped targets never authorize keyboard input to unrelated siblings or silently switch to another sibling after closing.

windows.identity: foregroundSelector includes NativeWindowHandle, with exact Name/ClassName/ProcessId. Reuse this fresh object in guarded scope or focus WindowSelectorJson, without treating it as ownership. Owned WindowIdentityJson presence/absence uses the native window lifetime token and process start time, so a disappearing UIA provider cannot cause false absence or a FromHandle cleanup race.
windows.notes: Native top-level enumeration includes owned/broker dialogs even when UIA nests them below an owner. ProcessId queries can additionally inspect provider-only modal descendants. Foreground inspects only the native foreground root, honors selector filters and TimeoutMs, and returns its fresh foregroundSelector; count 0 means the expected window never appeared. After submit use Foreground with the tested WindowTitle and a bounded wait before guarded input. Pass that observed selector to WindowSelectorJson; it is required for ForegroundWindow scope. Do not assume the broker shares the application's PID. Bare Foreground is only a snapshot. Foreground cannot combine with Checkpoint or WindowIdentityJson. Checkpoint records all native handles for new-window ownership; WindowIdentityJson verifies one exact owned receipt. After closing, use WaitForNotExists with an explicit selector (prefer the exact owned WindowIdentityJson); conditionMet confirms absence and returns immediately when gone. Without this flag, TimeoutMs waits for appearance and wastes the deadline after closure. Absence cannot combine with Foreground/Checkpoint and fails on incomplete enumeration. File/content checks need their own observations.

observe.usage: observe [-Format Compact|Full] [-Scope Working|FocusedWindow|ForegroundWindow] [-WindowSelectorJson <exact window identity>] [<selector options>] [-Depth 2] [-MaxElements 120]
observe.brokerScope: For an observed system-hosted dialog, first windows -Foreground if its identity is unknown. Scope ForegroundWindow accepts exact observed WindowSelectorJson Name/ClassName (optional ProcessId/NativeWindowHandle), plus FallbackReason/FallbackEvidence. It supports observe/select/read/wait-element/click/type/press-key without a working window or host ownership. Focused typing additionally requires ExpectedFocusJson. Input checks the guarded foreground root and native focus; it never changes the working window. Ordinary FocusedWindow remains owner-restricted.
observe.notes: Compact returns actionable flat elements, focusedElement, live bounds, patterns and candidate selectors; check uniqueness before acting. Full (CLI default) preserves the nested tree. FocusedWindow inspects the owned foreground window. Name/SelectorJson/PathJson can anchor a subtree. Depth 0..20, MaxElements 1..2000. limitReached means the node budget was exhausted; depthBoundaryReached means descendants at the depth boundary were not inspected (not proof that they exist). A missing control in a bounded tree is not proof of UIA absence. Before coordinate fallback, scope deeper discovery to an observed container or search a short label fragment with select -Name '*fragment*' -TimeoutMs 0. Opaque Pane roles can change as providers initialize.

select.providerFallback: A filtered lookup miss inside an application subtree is retried with the same unfiltered child traversal as observe, using unchanged local matching. Traversal is bounded to 1500 nodes/1500 ms/32 levels and never expands the desktop; SearchIncomplete requires a narrower PathJson scope, not guessed coordinates. InteractiveOnly filters visible enabled controls locally and is useful for wait-element before submitting a dialog.
select.notes: Queries elements; it does not select a dropdown item. data.count=0 is a valid query result. Open a dropdown before looking for its items. Use SelectorJson with a Name array for alternative labels in one query; TimeoutMs 0 is useful for discovery. Scope FocusedWindow searches the owned foreground dialog without relying on IsModal. Add role/class constraints only to disambiguate, especially for opaque Pane controls.

click.doubleClick: ClickCount 2 forces one atomic physical double-click using live target geometry; it rejects Method Invoke. Use this for an observed double-click route instead of separate CLI calls. A requested menu path still needs that exact menu path, even when double-click opens the same file.
click.focusBehavior: Auto/Invoke dispatch the supported action without first focusing the parent or item, which can dismiss a popup or alter selection. Focus and ElementFocus now default false for semantic actions. Mouse fallback activates the target's actual window only when needed; an already active owned popup is preserved. Explicit Focus/ElementFocus overrides remain available. Visible/enabled eligibility and uniqueness are checked from live properties, including providers with inconsistent compound search filters. TargetNotFound means no input was dispatched.
click.usage: click <selector options> [-RequireUnique true] [-Method Auto|Mouse|Invoke] [-ClickCount 1|2] [-RelativeX 0.5 -RelativeY 0.5] [-Center true] [-Button Left|Right] [-Focus false] [-ElementFocus false] [-OffsetX 0] [-OffsetY 0] [-VerifyDisappeared]
click.notes: Use default Auto: native push buttons use physical mouse input to avoid synchronous UIA Invoke/BM_CLICK errors (0x8001010D) in file dialogs; other controls use supported UIA patterns then mouse fallback. RequireUnique defaults true: multiple visible enabled matches fail before input with error.candidates. Add an observed ID, role, class or parent scope; do not blindly choose the first label. RequireUnique false explicitly restores legacy first-match behavior. Explicit Invoke is checked before changing focus and requires InvokePattern, but can still trigger input-synchronous call errors; use Auto or Mouse for native submit buttons. Scope FocusedWindow targets controls in the owned foreground dialog. Mouse uses live geometry. RelativeX/Y select a point within live bounds (fractions 0..1, both required) and force mouse input; do not combine with offsets/Center/Invoke. For menus already open, Focus false and ElementFocus false avoid changing focus before the click. Observe the postcondition before retrying.

click-coordinate.notes: Fallback only; retain a screenshot and explain the missing selector route. For an observed double-click route, use ClickCount 2 on click (preferred live selector) or click-coordinate: both presses are inserted in one native input sequence. Do not emulate a double-click with separate tool/CLI commands. Double-click forces mouse input; Method Invoke is rejected. This does not replace a specific menu route required by the CSV. Inspect the postcondition; no fallback action is retried after failed input.

type.acknowledgement: PreDelete plus exact Verify on a readable single-line standard Edit acknowledges each Unicode scalar from actual Win32 text before sending the next, including InputDelayMs 0. data.consumptionAcknowledged identifies this path. Other editors keep paced final readback. TextConsumptionFailed stops the unsent suffix after a 500 ms prefix deadline and returns error.textReadback (bounded observedText/lengths); it never retypes. Missing letters/separators are input loss, not proof of extension/path normalization. Inspect actual text before a targeted correction. Automatic acknowledgement applies only to replacement fields, not rich/opaque editors, password/multiline controls or append typing.
type.pacing: Omit InputDelayMs initially: acknowledged standard Edit replacement defaults to consumption feedback with no blind sleep; other editors default to 5 ms per Unicode scalar. InputDelayMs accepts 0..100 and explicit delays are honored. Outside the acknowledged path, 0 opts into bursts for a route tested to tolerate them. Legacy TypeByCharacter means 50 ms and cannot be combined with InputDelayMs. Surrogate pairs stay together. Native focus is rechecked during typing; a change aborts remaining text and reports partial dispatch as unknown. No text is resent automatically. Use Verify/readback to detect lost text; a successful SendInput is queue insertion, not proof of consumption. Preserve tested pacing in generated scripts.
type.focusInput: Focused means unscoped keyboard input at the existing owned foreground target. It does not require an editable UIA role or a true UIA HasKeyboardFocus flag: Win32 keyboard focus corroborates custom canvases whose accessibility provider disagrees. No focus changes are made. Selection is preserved unless PreDelete explicitly requests supported UIA/native text selection. FocusTimeoutMs defaults to 2000 even without ExpectedFocusJson. Optional ExpectedFocusJson matches the reported UIA target or actual native focus control, not an arbitrary unfocused selector. data.inputFocus reports the source and native identity; failures expose error.focus with outcome not-dispatched. Use the observed identity after a dialog/menu transition to avoid typing into another owned control. A ready keyboard target does not prove a text-edit caret or successful content entry; assert the result.
type.usage: type -Text 'literal text' [-PathKind SaveFile|OpenFile|Directory] [<selector options>] [-TargetMode Writable|Focused] [-ExpectedFocusJson <identity selector> -FocusTimeoutMs 2000] [-FallbackReason <reason> -FallbackEvidence <reference>] [-FocusMethod Auto|UIA|Mouse] [-PreDelete] [-ClearMethod Selection|Shortcut] [-Verify] [-VerifyMode Exact|Contains|NormalizedExact|NormalizedContains] [-VerifyTimeoutMs 3000] [-MaxAttempts 0] [-InputDelayMs 5 | -TypeByCharacter] [-Focus]
type.pathInput: For filename fields use PathKind SaveFile (existing parent directory), OpenFile (existing file), or Directory (existing directory). Requires an absolute drive or UNC path with backslash separators; use Join-Path. Forward slashes accepted by filesystem APIs can be rejected by GUI filename fields. Checks the literal Text before focus, clearing, or typing; PathValidationFailed means not-dispatched. No files/directories are created and Text is never trimmed, expanded, or rewritten. Preserve the full path, including spaces and Unicode; do not copy a shortened UI label or insert quote characters around Text. This validates the supplied path, not field readback, save permission, or the application's save result. Verify readback when supported and assert wait-file after the visible save action. PathKind defaults Verify to true with exact readback. Standard Windows Edit controls support native readback/selection even when UIA reports Pane and no patterns; text still enters through keyboard events, never WM_SETTEXT. An explicit -Verify false skips readback only for a tested commit-on-exit route with a separate assertion. If text is lost, inspect/reset the field and test slower InputDelayMs; do not shorten the path or assume its current directory.
type.notes: Literal Unicode keyboard input, never clipboard. Writable mode is default and checks UIA/native writability and native-confirmed focus; selector Auto focus falls back to a visible click. Multiline literals require a writable Document target, not a nested single-line Edit. Focused mode is an explicit audited fallback for an observed opaque editor: existing focus only, no target selector/refocus/newlines/tabs, and explicit read-only still fails. ExpectedFocusJson optionally waits for observed focus identity and owned foreground readiness without clicking/refocusing or losing an existing selection; FocusTimeoutMs is 0..10000. It is a guard, not a focus action. Both modes check the actual foreground application or owned dialog. Verify polls current readback without resending or committing. For commit-on-exit controls, type once without Verify, commit through an observed control or permitted press-key Enter, then read/assert. Normalized modes reconcile line endings. TimeoutMs is lookup time; VerifyTimeoutMs is readback time. For replacement prefer writable PreDelete plus Verify; PreDelete skips clearing when actual readback is empty; otherwise it uses TextPattern or standard Windows Edit selection and keyboard Backspace, also in Focused mode. Unsupported selection returns TextSelectionUnavailable before text input. Do not click an already selected filename just to wait for focus. Shortcut clearing requires authorization.

press-key.focusInput: Uses the same native-confirmed owned keyboard target as focused typing. FocusTimeoutMs is 0..10000, default 2000. UIA focus disagreement alone does not block navigation. Ownership is rechecked before each key; a partially dispatched sequence still has outcome unknown on failure.
press-key.notes: GuiNavigation/AllowShortcuts only. Sends bounded navigation to confirmed focus in the working application or its owned dialog and returns focus before/after. afterError reports an optional post-input provider readback failure without invalidating sent=true; inspect the actual postcondition before retrying. Count is 1..20; Enter/Escape must be single actions followed by an observation. No application hotkeys, function keys, clipboard, key expressions, or implicit refocus. Required menu/button routes still apply. Dispatch does not verify the application postcondition.

hotkey.notes: Disabled by default, including Enter confirmations. One chord only, no grouped sequences or clipboard shortcuts. Requires user/testcase permission.

drag.notes: Click/hold, move, and drop using checked SendInput mouse events in physical virtual-desktop coordinates. Each endpoint can be a selector (including nested paths) or coordinates. Resolves both visible/enabled controls before pressing; a missing endpoint has outcome not-dispatched. Fractions choose a point inside current element bounds; defaults are centers. Smooth motion uses native elapsed-time interpolation; DurationMs is 50..10000. Always attempts button release after pressing, including failure. released/dragged mean input delivery; assert the actual drop result separately. Coordinate endpoints need observed fallback evidence.

wait-element.notes: Assert data.exists, not just ok. Presence waits stop at the first match and include the application/scope root; use select for match counts. A control wait behind a disabled working window and confirmed owned foreground modal fails early with WaitBlockedByDialog and error.blockingDialog.foregroundSelector. Inspect the actual dialog before recovery. Use TimeoutMs; scoped waits allow 0..60000 ms. Scope FocusedWindow/ForegroundWindow waits tolerate a temporarily different foreground owner/guard and refresh the root until the deadline. data.lastScopeError explains an unmet ownership/guard condition. Invalid selectors still fail immediately. Add InteractiveOnly for a visible enabled submit control. A launched window does not prove blank document state or readiness.

wait-file.notes: Assert data.conditionMet. StableMs requires unchanged length AND last-write time. Directories are not files. Stability alone does not prove file validity or content. Use unique execution paths to avoid stale-file passes.

read.notes: Returns data.text and data.textSource (ValuePattern, TextPattern, or Name fallback). Content assertions require a text pattern; an element name proves only its label. After reopening, read the document control and assert every required content fragment. Use read, not empty typing, to observe text.

read-pdf.imageContent: This command extracts text, not rendered images. An image-only PDF can be valid and still have no extractable text. For image/layout/cropping expectations render the actual PDF with an available verified renderer and assert/inspect its pixels; retain that check in replay. A binary header or non-white bounds alone cannot prove the complete required image. OCR is relevant only when actual text must be extracted.
read-pdf.fileRead: The built-in reader takes a read-only shared snapshot, allowing a print/export producer to retain its write handle. It detects size/timestamp changes during copying. Both readers require a final PDF EOF marker and retry transient sharing/lock violations within TimeoutMs (0..60000, default 5000); malformed/unsupported PDFs are not repeatedly retried. Keep wait-file MinBytes and a short StableMs before reading. A zero-byte/spooling file still requires a bounded producer wait, not repeated input or longer waits in every future script.
read-pdf.notes: Read-only text extraction; returns data.path, data.text, and data.reader. Auto tries the built-in simple PDF reader, then optional installed Python+pypdf if PythonPath or POTATO_PDF_PYTHON is configured. The shipped helper avoids inline-code quoting and never creates expected outputs. Builtin has no dependencies but rejects object/xref streams and other unsupported layouts. Neither reader performs OCR; missing/empty text fails. No desktop or session-state mutation.

screenshot.notes: Returns physical-pixel imageWidth/imageHeight, region and coordinateSpace. Inspect original pixels before coordinates; add region.x/y to image pixel coordinates. After opaque asynchronous actions, WaitForChangeFrom waits for an observed content region to change from a prior original PNG capture and settle, then saves that final frame once. ChangeRegionJson is required in image pixels; exclude focus/hover/caret indicators and unrelated animation. Reference and capture must have identical dimensions/origin; lossy/resized references are unsuitable. Assert data.conditionMet; an unmet wait retains the final frame and never repeats input. Uses a bounded 64x64 RGB sample grid, so tiny changes can be missed. Change/stability is readiness, not expected-content verification. Without this option capture stays immediate. Capture alone is not an assertion.

close-window.closeBehavior: Native windows receive an asynchronous WM_CLOSE request so a close/save prompt cannot block the CLI inside WindowPattern.Close. Process identity is checked before posting; no force-kill or prompt suppression. data.closeRequested and legacy data.closed count requests, not completed exits. CLI ownership context remains available for prompt recovery. Verify closure separately. Provider-only windows without a native handle still use WindowPattern.Close.
close-window.notes: With no selector, targets only the working window. A ProcessId query includes nested modal windows and closes them before the parent. An explicit selector miss never closes another working window. data.closed counts accepted close requests; inspect remaining windows for cleanup verification. For shared hosts use WindowIdentityJson from the ownership receipt. Only that still-matching window is closed; unrelated windows and the host process are preserved. Pending save prompts remain visible and cleanup reports failure until resolved.

report.notes: Records a report event; it does not validate that the status is justified.

globalOptions.InteractionPolicy: GuiNavigation (default), VisibleControls (strict), or explicitly authorized AllowShortcuts
globalOptions.FallbackReason: Required explanation for focused opaque typing, press-key, and authorized shortcuts
globalOptions.FallbackEvidence: Required observation/screenshot reference for focused opaque typing, press-key, and authorized shortcuts
